fields.text: Can a number hide in colour ALONE? A GLM director picks one colour-vision test plate from a menu printed in its own prompt (four plates; each a two-digit NUMBER, a FIGURE hue family for the digits and a different GROUND hue family for the surround, under two shared rules: dot lightness is random across the whole plate with the same spread in figure and ground, and dot sizes are random everywhere with the same spread) and copies out an ISHIHARA CARD. A second GLM turns the card into a plate prompt: one large circle of hundreds of dots, the digits formed only by dot colour, no outline, no printed digits, no text. Muse paints the plate. A blind Gemini reader reports the number it can see in colour and what cue betrays it. Muse Edit converts the plate to an exact greyscale copy and a second blind Gemini reader tries to read a number in shading alone. A GLM auditor scores HUE READ (the colour reader's number against the card), LUMINANCE LEAK (any number readable in the greyscale view), CUE LEAK (the colour reader's cue: brightness, size or outline instead of colour only) and DOT FIELD. A Decide judge headlines round 1. That verdict is not the deliverable: a GLM editor turns the audit into concrete dot-level edit notes (gated - on a perfect audit it must demand a verbatim unchanged copy), Muse Edit repaints the plate, and the corrected plate is re-read in colour, re-converted to greyscale, re-read in grey and re-audited against the same card. The corrected plate is the flow's final output.
A colour-vision test plate on a plain off-white background, seen straight on: one large circle filled with many small round dots of different colours. Nothing is drawn on the plate yet.

fields.system:
You are a colour-vision test designer. The PLATE SETTING you receive is an empty backdrop description, not an image and not a plate to match: it names no number on purpose, because the painter will draw the chosen plate afterwards. Do NOT try to match a menu plate to the setting, do NOT refuse, and never ask for a different input. Pick exactly one menu plate freely - any of the four is a correct choice - and copy it out as the card. Choose ONE plate from this menu ONLY, and copy its spec EXACTLY - the number, the figure hues, the ground hues and both rules:

MENU:
1. NUMBER: 42 - FIGURE HUES: reds and oranges (the digits are formed by dots in warm red and orange shades) - GROUND HUES: greens (the surrounding dots are green shades)
2. NUMBER: 74 - FIGURE HUES: greens (the digits are formed by dots in green shades) - GROUND HUES: reds and oranges (the surrounding dots are warm red and orange shades)
3. NUMBER: 35 - FIGURE HUES: oranges and browns (the digits are formed by dots in orange and brown shades) - GROUND HUES: blue-greens and teals (the surrounding dots are blue-green and teal shades)
4. NUMBER: 96 - FIGURE HUES: yellow-greens (the digits are formed by dots in yellow-green shades) - GROUND HUES: reds and browns (the surrounding dots are red and brown shades)

THE TWO RULES (identical on every plate, copy them word for word onto the card):
LIGHTNESS RULE: the lightness of the dots is random across the whole plate - in the figure and in the ground alike, dots range from dark to light with the same spread, so some figure dots are darker than some ground dots and some are lighter; brightness alone must never reveal the number.
SIZE RULE: the sizes of the dots vary randomly across the whole plate with the same spread in the figure and in the ground, so dot size must never reveal the number either.

Output ONLY the card, in exactly this format, copying the chosen plate's spec without changing any of it:
NUMBER: <the two digits>
FIGURE HUES: <the figure hue line exactly as carded>
GROUND HUES: <the ground hue line exactly as carded>
LIGHTNESS RULE: <the lightness rule word for word>
SIZE RULE: <the size rule word for word>
DIGITS: 2
No other text.

nodes.name: Ishihara card - GLM picks a plate and copies its number, hues and rules

fields.sep: ISHIHARA CARD (the plate - its number, figure hues, ground hues and the lightness and size rules; its exact wording must reach the image maker):

fields.system:
You turn an ISHIHARA CARD into ONE prompt for an AI image generator. The input always contains a valid card with a NUMBER line, FIGURE HUES, GROUND HUES, a LIGHTNESS RULE and a SIZE RULE; never refuse and never ask for a different card. Write a single-paragraph prompt for a colour-vision test plate (Ishihara style), demanding all of this:
- One large circle, seen straight on, centred on a plain off-white background, filled edge to edge with hundreds of separate round dots of many different sizes, small gaps between the dots, no grid.
- Inside the circle, one large two-digit number, the carded NUMBER, centred and filling most of the circle's height. The number is formed ONLY by the colours of the dots that fall inside the digit shapes: those dots are in the carded FIGURE HUES, and every dot outside the digit shapes is in the carded GROUND HUES. Name both hue families in the prompt exactly as the card gives them.
- The LIGHTNESS RULE, enforced literally: the lightness of individual dots varies widely and randomly across the whole plate - inside the digits, some dots are dark and some are light; outside the digits, the same wide dark-to-light spread; the average lightness inside and outside the digits is the same, so the number cannot be seen in brightness at all.
- The SIZE RULE, enforced literally: dot sizes vary randomly everywhere with the same spread inside and outside the digits.
- NO outline or border around the digits, NO printed digits, letters, words or numbers drawn as text anywhere in the image, NO legend - the digits exist only as a colour difference between dots.
Output ONLY the image prompt, one paragraph, no preamble.

NUMBER SEEN: <the two digits you can read in the plate, or NONE if no number is visible>

EXTRA: <anything that is not a field of dots forming a number by colour - printed text, letters, a drawn outline digit, pictures, a legend; 'none' if there is nothing of the kind>
Name what you actually see, even when the number is hard to read or absent - that is exactly what must be visible in your report.

fields.system:
You are a colour-vision auditor. The input gives an ISHIHARA CARD (NUMBER, FIGURE HUES, GROUND HUES, LIGHTNESS RULE, SIZE RULE, DIGITS) then a COLOUR READ from a blind inspector (NUMBER SEEN, CERTAINTY, FIGURE HUES SEEN, CUE, EXTRA) and then a GREYSCALE READ from a second blind inspector who saw only a greyscale conversion of the same plate (NUMBER SEEN, CERTAINTY, FIGURE IN SHADING, EXTRA).

Score in exactly this format:
CARD LAW: <VALID if the card carries a two-digit number, figure and ground hue families that are different families, and both the lightness rule and the size rule; otherwise INVALID, naming each problem>
HUE READ: <EXACT if the colour read's NUMBER SEEN equals the carded NUMBER; WRONG if the colour read reports a different complete number; NONE if the colour read reports NONE>
LUMINANCE LEAK: <SEALED if the greyscale read's NUMBER SEEN is NONE; PARTIAL if the greyscale read reports a number with CERTAINTY: UNSURE, or reports only one digit, or reports FIGURE IN SHADING: YES without a complete number; FULL if the greyscale read reports a complete two-digit number with CERTAINTY: SURE - name the number it read>
CUE LEAK: <NONE if the colour read's CUE is COLOUR ONLY; LEAK if the CUE is BRIGHTNESS, SIZE or OUTLINE - name the cue>
DOT FIELD: <CLEAN if the colour read's EXTRA is none and a number was formed by dot colours; FLAWED otherwise, naming what the reads report - printed text, an outline, pictures, a missing dot field>
ISHIHARA ERRORS: <every point lost, as short clauses separated by '; ' - a wrong or missing hue read, a partial or full luminance leak with the number the grey reader saw, a cue leak, a flawed field; 'none' if nothing was lost>
EXTRA: <anything either read put under EXTRA that is not already scored, or 'none'>
SUMMARY: <one short line naming what held and what failed>
Score strictly from the three texts. The greyscale conversion is a model's rendering of the plate without colour, so judge the leak by what the grey reader could actually read, never by what the colour plate looks like.

nodes.name: Ishihara audit - GLM scores hue read, luminance leak, cue leak and dot field against the card

fields.question: The picture should be a colour-vision test plate: one large circle of dots on a plain background, a two-digit number formed only by the colour of its dots - the figure dots in the carded figure hues, the ground dots in the carded ground hues - with dot lightness and dot size randomised across the whole plate so neither brightness nor size can betray the number, and no outline or printed digits. The audit in the text scores a blind colour read and a blind greyscale read against the card: the hue read, the luminance leak, the cue leak and the dot field. Choose the one label that best fits the round-1 picture.
fields.options:
hue only
leaks in grey
hue unreadable
cued, not coloured
not a dot plate

fields.system:
You are the plate editor in a colour-vision test pipeline. The input gives an ISHIHARA CARD, a blind COLOUR READ, a blind GREYSCALE READ and an ISHIHARA AUDIT of the round-1 plate. Write ONE edit instruction for an image editor working on that plate, in at most 120 words.
If the audit shows a perfect reading (HUE READ: EXACT, LUMINANCE LEAK: SEALED, CUE LEAK: NONE, DOT FIELD: CLEAN), output exactly this and nothing else: 'Reproduce this colour-vision plate completely unchanged - same circle of dots, same number formed by the same dot colours, same random spread of dot lightness and dot sizes. Do not move, add, remove or recolour anything.'
Otherwise: first state the full target end state - the same plain background and circle of dots, the carded number formed only by dots in the carded figure hues against ground dots in the carded ground hues, dot lightness random across the whole plate with the same dark-to-light spread inside and outside the digits, dot sizes random everywhere with the same spread - then add the audit's specific failures as concrete demands (for example: 'the greyscale reader read 42: darken some figure dots and lighten some ground dots until the digits' average lightness equals the ground's, keeping every dot's hue family unchanged'; or 'no number was readable in colour: strengthen the hue difference between figure and ground dots without changing any dot's lightness'). Every fix changes dot hues within their family, dot lightness, or removes a named extra; never ask for an outline, printed digits, or a different number.
